title: The reusable descent step for sums of two squares
statement: Let m be nonzero, let m*p = a^2 + b^2 and m*q = c^2 + e^2, and suppose the two cross terms of the conjugate Brahmagupta grouping are divisible by m with quotients u and w, so that m*u = a*c + b*e and m*w = a*e - b*c. Then q*p = u^2 + w^2. The multiplier drops from m to q and the conclusion has the SAME SHAPE as the first hypothesis, so an induction on a Nat measure of the multiplier applies directly. The quotients u and w are hypotheses rather than constructions: exhibiting them is what F:int-two-squares-descent-cross-terms licenses, and leaving them quantified keeps this step usable by any descent that can produce them, not only the balanced-representative one.

formal.statement: theorem Int.descentStep : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : Int) -> ((x3 : Int) -> ((x4 : Int) -> ((x5 : Int) -> ((x6 : Int) -> ((x7 : Int) -> ((x8 : Int) -> ((x9 : Not (Eq.{1} Int x0 Int.zero)) -> ((x10 : Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul x0 x1) (Int.add (Int.mul x3 x3) (Int.mul x4 x4))) -> ((x11 : Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul x0 x2) (Int.add (Int.mul x5 x5) (Int.mul x6 x6))) -> ((x12 : Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul x0 x7) (Int.add (Int.mul x3 x5) (Int.mul x4 x6))) -> ((x13 : Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul x0 x8) (Int.sub (Int.mul x3 x6) (Int.mul x4 x5))) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul x2 x1) (Int.add (Int.mul x7 x7) (Int.mul x8 x8))))))))))))))))

evidence.notes: Two independent failure modes, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing: int_theorem_inventory exits non-zero when the named filter matches nothing, and grep -c exits 1 printing 0 when the anchored line is absent. Anchored with [[:space:]] and never with a backslash-t, which a scripted (GNU) grep reads as a literal t. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this tool builds the constructed carriers and overflows the default debug thread stack. The anchor AFTER the name is load-bearing here, because Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci' is a different declaration whose rendered name has Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci as a prefix.

notes: Multiplicative cancellation over the integers had to be BUILT for this: shape_search --ns Int --name-contains cancel found only additive and ModEq cancellations, so Int.mul_left_cancel_of_ne_zero was derived from Int.mul_eq_zero, together with Int.mul_ne_zero, Int.eq_of_sub_eq_zero, Int.zero_add, Int.sub_self, Int.add_sub_cancel_right and Int.mul_sub_mul_comm. The worked instance in the test battery is the p = 13 descent: 5^2 + 1^2 = 26 = 2*13, balanced representatives c = e = 1, new multiplier q = 1, quotients u = 3 and w = 2, conclusion 1*13 = 3^2 + 2^2. Its negative halves are u = 2 and w = 3, both refused. That the conclusion is q*p and NOT m*p -- the entire content of calling this a descent -- is pinned by the_descent_step_concludes_at_the_new_multiplier, since at that instance 1*13 checks and 2*13 does not.
